extracted.intended_audience: Patent examiners of ASEAN IP offices; patent applicants, agents and professional advisors filing in ASEAN Member States
extracted.subtask_description: Common Guidelines for substantive and formal patent examination across ASEAN Member States covering filing, formalities, publication, search, patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability), claim clarity, amendments, and work-sharing (ASPEC/PCT-ASPEC). Intended to guide examiners re-using other AMS work products and to inform applicants/agents filing across AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must file their patent application, including the specification, in the official language of the country of filing (or English where permitted). The language of filing is used as the language of the proceedings and for any amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed in a language other than an official/authorized language, a translation of the specification (title, abstract, claims, description and drawings) must be filed within a specified period or upon request of the patent office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents and information required for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific documents and information that must accompany a patent filing (e.g., specification, claims, abstract, drawings, applicant details, priority documents where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements vary by AMS; the Guidelines list required filing documents per AMS and note that failure to provide required documents may affect filing date or require completion within set periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation, certification, notarization or legalization of filing documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on whether translations must be certified/notarized/legalized when filing documents in a non-official language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMS require certified translations or verification by a translator/agent; specifics differ across countries (see Chapter 1.3 and country notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Option and deadlines for late filing of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how applicants can submit missing or late documents after initial filing, and the maximum deadlines allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines summarise the availability of time limits and any fees or formal requirements for restoring or completing an application after late filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the specification — period for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is filed in a language other than required, a translation of the specification must be submitted within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period and consequences of non-compliance are AMS-specific; refer to paragraph 1.5 for country-by-country practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims from multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for claiming priority from multiple earlier applications (including order, evidence, and effect on entitlement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on formalities for claiming priority and documentation required to support multiple priority claims is provided (see Question 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of filing fees and fees per excess claims
rubrics_metrics.description: How filing fees are calculated — per application, per claim, or per excess claim beyond a threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines summarise AMS practices on fee calculation and where fees scale with claim count or excess claims; applicants should consult national fee schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and requirements for e-filing patent applications with AMS patent offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines note which AMS provide e-filing and any constraints or legal requirements for electronic submissions (see Question 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between patent types based on priority document
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules allowing conversion of a patent application into a patent/utility model/petty patent/simple patent/utility innovation based on an earlier priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures, timelines and effects of conversion are country-specific (see Question 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for prejudicial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and scope of a grace period that allows certain disclosures by the inventor/applicant not to be prejudicial to novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ACG-PE refines common practices where AMSs have similar approaches to grace periods and prejudicial disclosures; specifics differ by AMS (see Question 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required for formalities examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of information examiners require to conduct formalities checks (completeness, formal compliance, entitlement, priority evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.1 lists required data; examiners must verify filing date, applicant identity, documents, translations, and conformity with filing requirements before proceeding to substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejecting an application on formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal defects or omissions that can lead to rejection of a patent application at the formalities stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.2 provides examples of grounds for rejection and indicates whether rejection is absolute or can be remedied within a time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of application before/during formalities examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and procedures allowing applicants to amend applications prior to or during the formalities examination stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.3 explains permissible amendments, timelines, and whether amended documents must be re-certified or re-translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of application after formalities examination
rubrics_metrics.description: How and on what grounds an applicant may amend an application after completion of formalities examination (other than to conform to the formalities report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.4 describes post-formalities amendment scope, fees, and any limitations tied to substantive examination issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic or paper filing of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether amendments are accepted electronically or must be paper-filed, and any formal requirements for each mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.5 summarises AMS practices; some offices accept e-amendments, others require paper or specific forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and method used to assess whether the claims relate to a single general inventive concept (unity of invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.6 and Chapter 6 define unity, explain assessment in light of prior art, and provide procedures for raising objections and dividing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing filing of divisional applications derived from a parent application (timing, subject-matter, and scope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.7 sets out when division is permitted, time limits, and effects on filing date and priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for foreign filing licence before foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessity of obtaining government authorization (foreign filing licence) before filing a patent abroad for inventions subject to national security/export control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.8 explains which AMS require such licences and the administrative steps to obtain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordal of changes (name, address, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for recording changes in applicant/owner name, address or other bibliographic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.9 explains documentary proof required, fees, and effects on file status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application before formalities examination
rubrics_metrics.description: How applicants may withdraw their application prior to formalities examination and the consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.10 summarises withdrawal procedures, restoration possibilities, and fee implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rejection or abandonment of the priority application
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences for subsequent applications when the priority application is rejected or abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.11 addresses how loss of priority affects patentability and available remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure for formalities objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and/or judicial procedures available to challenge formalities-based rejections or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2.12 outlines appeal routes, timelines, and requirements for filing appeals in AMSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how patent applications are published (e.g., 18 months from priority) and what is disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.1 provides publication timing, contents, and relation to national rules; includes references to possible deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delaying or expediting publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Possibility and procedures to delay (e.g., request non-publication) or expedite publication of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.2 describes conditions and mechanisms for early or deferred publication where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information published in patent gazette/bulletin
rubrics_metrics.description: The types of bibliographic and procedural information included in official patent publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.3 lists typical contents: title, abstract, claims, figures, applicant/agent names, and legal status events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims of published applications
rubrics_metrics.description: How and when claims can be amended after publication but before grant, and the required procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.4 explains amendment filings, effect on public record, and where re-publication may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of granted patent specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for publishing the granted patent text/specification and related bibliographic details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.5 sets out the timing and format of post-grant publication and notice to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and re-publication of granted patents for mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Process for correcting mistakes in granted patents and republishing corrected texts when errors are attributable to applicant or office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.6 details correction procedures, classification of errors, and resubmission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration, format and language(s) of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing the term/duration, official format and languages used for published patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.7 summarises national practices and any obligations to provide translations for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between patent and petty patent/utility model before/during/after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how an application may be converted between full patent and petty patent/utility model at different stages of prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.8 explains timing constraints, formalities and effects on examination and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights upon publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether publication confers provisional rights on the applicant/owner (e.g., damages after grant for uses after publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3.9 discusses national positions on provisional protection upon publication and relevant legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination — availability and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether substantive examination is conducted and the time limit to file a request for substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.1–4.2 explain which AMS conduct substantive examination and the deadlines and conditions to request it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of substantive examination by the office of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: How the local patent office performs substantive examination, including scope, standards and use of external reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.3 outlines examination procedures, reliance options on other offices, and internal practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for applicants as to which office conducts substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Choices available to applicants regarding which patent office will perform substantive examination (e.g., requesting examination by another office or using ASPEC/PCT results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.4 lists available options, procedural steps and implications for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive issues examined (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, clarity, sufficiency, exclusions) and limits of examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.5 clarifies whether the office examines both formal and substantive patentability criteria and any scope limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for expediting substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms (e.g., ASPEC AIM, PPH-like schemes, accelerated examination requests) to accelerate substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.6 explains available acceleration routes, eligibility (e.g., allowable claims in a first office), and required documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of patentability of subject matter during formalities/substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how patentability (including statutory subject-matter exclusions) may be assessed during formalities or only during substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.7 discusses practices across AMS and when examination of subject-matter exclusions may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of substantive examination reports to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether substantive examination reports are published/made accessible to third parties and under what conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.8 summarises AMS policies on public disclosure of examination reports and best practices (e.g., online registers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of substantive examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures, grounds and timelines for appealing substantive rejections or examination reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.9–4.11 explain appeal rights, form and content of reports, and language considerations for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-grant and post-grant opposition actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability, grounds, parties entitled, timelines, and procedures for opposition actions both pre-grant and post-grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.12–4.17 provide the framework for opposition proceedings, including opportunities to respond and appeal options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of foreign office decisions in opposition actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and to what extent decisions of foreign patent offices are considered in opposition actions for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.18 indicates that offices may consider foreign decisions as persuasive but retain autonomy in final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party submissions before and during substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules allowing third parties to submit prior art or observations and the timing and format for such submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4.19 outlines admissibility, confidentiality, and procedural effects of third-party observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of invention and statutory subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes an invention and what subject-matter is statutory or excluded (discoveries, theories, mathematical methods, business methods, aesthetic creations, presentation of information, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5.1–5.2 list exclusions and provide explanation and examples for each excluded category (see subparts 5.2.1–5.2.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of computer programs and business methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach to assessing patentability of computer programs, schemes/rules for business methods, and methods for performing purely mental acts or playing games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5.2.2 and 5.2.6 discuss tests for technical contribution and eligibility, referencing PCT/ EPO approaches and ASEAN common practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical methods, surgical/therapeutic and diagnostic method exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether methods for treatment of humans/animals by surgery, therapy or diagnosis are excluded from patentability and how such claims are treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5.2.7 explains national positions and permissible claim drafting (e.g., use claims, medical use claims) across AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plants, animals and essentially biological processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability of plants, animals and biological processes for production of plants/animals and related exclusions/limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5.2.8 sets out how AMS treat biological subject-matter and any statutory exclusions or special regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceutical products, drugs and foodstuffs considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: How pharmaceutical products and related inventions are treated with respect to patentability, safety, public order and regulatory interplay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5.2.10 discusses particular considerations in assessing patentability for pharmaceuticals and related disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and evaluation of unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies the definition of 'unity of invention' and provides evaluation criteria and assessment methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 6.1–6.3 explain unity assessment including relationship to prior art, and Chapter 6.4 covers appeal mechanisms on unity objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity requirements for claims and description
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions necessary for clarity of the invention in claims and description; claims must be clear and supported by description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7 (7.1–7.11) lists clarity conditions, prohibited terms, rules for drawings, multiple dependencies, one-part/two-part claim forms, multiple independent claims, use claims, product-by-process claims, ranges, limitations, disclaimers, and imprecise terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for drawings and figures in relation to clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for drawings and figures to support claims and description with respect to clarity requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7.3 specifies formatting, labelling, and how drawings interact with descriptions and claims to meet clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependencies and multiple independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissibility and treatment of multiple dependent claims and multiple independent claims in the same application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters 7.4 and 7.6 explain limitations, allowable forms and how such claims affect fees, unity and clarity assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requirement — claims must be supported by description and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims (independent and dependent) need to be supported by disclosure in the description and drawings; lack of support is a ground for objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is emphasised in Chapter 7 and reiterated in Chapters on sufficiency and amendments; amendments to claims may require corresponding description amendments (Chapter 7.14 / 13.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure / enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification must disclose the invention sufficiently to enable a person skilled in the art to carry it out without undue burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 8 addresses the need to substantiate the patent specification, required level of detail, examples, and consequences of insufficiency (lack of enablement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent search — options and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Search tools, databases and options available to applicants and examiners for prior art searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9.1–9.4 list typical databases used by AMS, language considerations, and sources (patent and non-patent literature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search parameters and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameters defining scope and thoroughness of the patent search (time periods, classification codes, document types), and coverage expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9.5 provides guidance on how to choose search parameters and what constitutes an appropriate search given resources and urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the closest prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and method to identify the 'closest prior art' for assessing inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9.6 explains selecting prior art most promising to assess inventive step and why this matters for problem-solution approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the search report
rubrics_metrics.description: What must be included in an office search report (citations, classifications, comments, relevance indication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9.7 describes typical contents and recommended formats for clarity and re-use (useful for ASPEC/WIPO CASE/Global Dossier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of partial search or 'no search' option
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an office may perform a partial search or issue a 'no search' due to lack of resources or for certain application types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9.8 describes conditions for partial/no search and how this should be communicated to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of novelty and novelty test
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'novelty' and the tests applied to determine whether claimed subject-matter is novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 10.1–10.2 set out novelty definitions and approaches including absolute novelty, state of the art, technical equivalents and combination attacks (Chapter 10.3 series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date and person skilled in the art for novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for determining the relevant date to assess prior art and who counts as a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 10.3.6–10.3.7 address the assessment date (priority/filing) and how to characterise the skilled person and enabling disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step definition and tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of inventive step and methods to determine it, including problem-solution approaches and alternative tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11.1–11.2 and 11.2.2 present the test for inventive step, methods of determining it, and how to apply these methods in examination (including prior art selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of knowledge and definition of person skilled in the art for inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterisation of the person skilled in the art and the scope of their common general knowledge relevant to inventive step analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters 11.3–11.4 set out factors to define the skilled person, their problem-solving abilities, and how to model their knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations (objective indicia) in inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of secondary factors (commercial success, long-felt need, unexpected technical effect, copying) that may support or negate inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11.6 describes how to treat secondary considerations and provides examples of supportive and opposing evidence (11.6.1–11.6.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention must be capable of industrial application; tests and grounds for appealing rejections based on lack of industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 12.1–12.2 define industrial applicability and outline appeal grounds and evidentiary expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-grant and post-grant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing amendments to application documents before grant and after grant, including allowable scope and limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 13.1–13.2 detail procedures for pre- and post-grant amendments, timing, formalities and substantive constraints to avoid adding new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of allowable amendments and amendments vs corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between what amendments are allowed (e.g., for clarity, limitation) and what changes are treated as corrections; constraints to prevent adding subject-matter beyond the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 13.3–13.4 describe allowable amendment scope, the difference between amendment and correction, and applicable procedures/limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide work results from priority applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement/expectation to provide available search and examination work products from the priority application when requesting ASPEC reuse or acceleration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14.2 summarises obligations to provide prior work products and the documents typically required for ASPEC requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC work-sharing procedures and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules for requesting ASPEC acceleration/work-product sharing, required documents (written opinion/IPER/WO/ISA reports), and eligibility criteria (including at least one allowable claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters 14.3 and 14.4 set out ASPEC and PCT-ASPEC request procedures, documents required, local agent requirements, claims correspondence table, e-ASPEC options, and country-specific quirks (tables listing AMS requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional documents outside ASPEC requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances under which a second IP Office may request additional documents beyond the ASPEC minimum (e.g., certified translations, publication notices, payment receipts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14.4 lists examples: translator verification (Cambodia), proof of publication and payment receipts (Indonesia), Thai translation requirements, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-use of search and examination results of other offices and work sharing best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using search/examination work products from other offices (modified examination, unilateral use, regional PPH, validation), and best practices for offices to publish S&E outputs for examiner access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14.5 explains that many examiners use foreign reports to facilitate examination, recommends publication of S&E results (e.g., European Patent Register), and references WIPO CASE, Global Dossier and IP5 CCD as work-sharing enablers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of WIPO CASE and IP5 CCD for work sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational modes for participation in WIPO CASE (Accessing Office vs Providing Office) and the Common Citation Document's role in consolidating citation data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14.5 describes technical participation levels, benefits for examiners, and how these systems support global work sharing and access to prior art citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles for harmonisation and convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACG-PE aim to enhance transparency, predictability, facilitate work-sharing and promote consistent high quality of patent search and examination among AMSs in line with international best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction and Conclusion explain objectives: to guide examiners re-using other AMS results, support offices without national guidelines, serve applicants and agents, and act as a practical training tool; ACG-PE are based on PCT Guidelines and EPO best practices where appropriate.
